full_judgment:
5. The plaintiff's case is that after coming to a finding that the plaintiff's case was true, the learned Subordinate judge should not have dismissed the suit of the plaintiff on the ground of hardship, because of the fact, at the relevant time there was no hardship on the part of the defendants and they entered into a contract knowing fully well about the facts and circumstances prevailing in the country and in that view, it was urged that a decree for specific performance of contract ought to have been passed. As against the finding the learned Subordinate Judge as to the validity of the contract as also the money decree that has been passed a cross-objection has been filed by the defendants, who contended that the plaintiff's suit was not maintainable in view of the fact that the time was the essence of contract as also for the reason that the plaintiff's story of payment of Tk. 9,000/- or that the contract was for Tk. 40,000/- have not been substantiated. It has also been urged by the cross-objectors that the deed of agreement contained interpolations by addition of certain sentences inserting the story of delivery of possession in favour of the plaintiff and in view of this fraud the learned Advocate for the cross-objectors submits that the plaintiff has not come with clean hands and as such his suit should have been dismissed in toto. In view of the fact that the appeal and the cross-objection are with regard to the same transaction, we take up both the appeal and the cross-objection together and dispose them of by this judgment. 

 7. So far as the cross-objection is concerned Mr. M.H. Khandker the learned Advocate has raised several points. He has urged that time is the essence of the contract because in the deed of agreement it was clearly stated that the document was to be executed within one month and the document having not been executed within one month the plaintiff was not entitled to enforce the performance of the said agreement. He has drawn our attention to the deposition of the plaintiff and referred the relevant portion of the agreement by the defendants to prove that the kabala was to be executed within one month failing which the advance money will be forfeited and this one month having expired it should be taken that the time was the essence of contract and as such the plaintiff was not entitled to any relief as he came to court long after the expiry of the said period. Mr. Khandker has referred to several decisions to substantiate his case that time was essence of contract in the facts and circumstances of the case. But in view of the admission in the written statement to the effect. that the defendants requested the plaintiff to take suit property on payment of the consideration money even after the expiry of that period of one month would show that the parties did not consider the stipulation in the agreement to the effect that the kabala was to the executed within one month, otherwise, the advance money be forfeited to be the essence of the contract. As a matter of fact the parties did not adhere to the same but kept it open even after the expiry of the period mentioned in the agreement. In that view of the matter we do not think it necessary to refer to those decisions referred to by Mr. Khandker. It also transpires from the evidence of the parties that the time was not essence of contract. Defendant No. 1 has stated that they approached the plaintiff several times to have the kabala executed and registered. The condition of the country at that time also must be taken into consideration. It is also in evidence of the plaintiff that he approached the defendants, but the defendants did not dare to come out because of the circumstances prevailing in the country. At that time there was general strike and everything came to a standstill. In that view it was not possible to have the kabala executed and registered within one month. The parties by their conduct having extended the time it could not be said that time was the essence of the contract. With regard to the question of fraud and interpolation of the document as argued by Mr. Khandker, he submitted that in view of the fact that the question of delivery of possession has been inserted in the document subsequently, the plaintiff was not entitled to any relief on the basis of such a fraudulent kabala. We are not concerned with the question of delivery of possession of the plaintiff here. He has made out a case that the defendants wanted to sell property at Tk. 40,000/- out of which they took an advance of Tk. 9,000/- and executed a deed of agreement in favour of the plaintiff. The defendants have admitted that they executed the document due to hard pressure and the condition prevailing in the country at that time. On evidence the court below has accepted the plaintiff's case of consideration money being Tk. 40,000/- out of which an advance of Tk. 9,000/- was paid. The court has on the ground of hardship refused the specific performance of contract and rejected the prayer of the plaintiff for the specific performance. So far as the refund of consideration is concerned the court has held that in view of the fact that the time was not essence of contract the question of fraud does not arise, and the defendants received Tk. 9,000/- in 1971 and did not refund the same until now and as such he was liable to refund the same to the plaintiff. He has, however, considered that the value of the money has gone down more than 4 times. He therefore passed a decree against the defendants to refund 4 times the advanced amount to the plaintiff. We do not find any illegality in this order of the learned Subordinate Judge.
